items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: But Pannassié, as everyone knows, he's a strict traditionalist, you know.

ctx.x: of the bebop. And so I had another experience like that.

When I returned to Paris with Nat Cole, we were doing a concert at the Salle Pleyel, and we had a French group to come on before we came on, see. So they played a few tunes and the people didn't want to hear them, they wanted to hear Nat. And so they started booing the band, so the band stopped playing and booed the audience. You know. But Pannassié, as everyone knows, he's a strict traditionalist, you know. He opposes anything other than Dixieland, I imagine. This is where he's coming from. So everything else is…

But things move on, you know, we progress. So I think it's very shortsighted on his part to, you know. But anyway, I got a chance to see Kenny Clark, again, on this trip because I remember -- I've known Kenny for years when he -- I think he was playing with Edgar Hayes when I first met Kenny somewhere. I was in Cincinnati with Roy Eldridge, playing the Cotton Club, and this is where I first met Kenny.
